From b98def7ca6e152ee55e36863dddf6f41f12d1dc6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Liu Bo <bo.liu@linux.alibaba.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2018 01:59:48 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] Btrfs: bail out on error during replay_dir_deletes

If errors were returned by btrfs_next_leaf(), replay_dir_deletes needs
to bail out, otherwise @ret would be forced to be 0 after 'break;' and
the caller won't be aware of it.

Fixes: e02119d5a7b4 ("Btrfs: Add a write ahead tree log to optimize synchronous operations")
Reviewed-by: Nikolay Borisov <nborisov@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Liu Bo <bo.liu@linux.alibaba.com>
Signed-off-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>

diff --git a/fs/btrfs/tree-log.c b/fs/btrfs/tree-log.c
index c6bfa86e2f22..678154d4b78f 100644
--- a/fs/btrfs/tree-log.c
+++ b/fs/btrfs/tree-log.c
@@ -2352,8 +2352,10 @@ static noinline int replay_dir_deletes(struct btrfs_trans_handle *trans,
 			nritems = btrfs_header_nritems(path->nodes[0]);
 			if (path->slots[0] >= nritems) {
 				ret = btrfs_next_leaf(root, path);
-				if (ret)
+				if (ret == 1)
 					break;
+				else if (ret < 0)
+					goto out;
 			}
 			btrfs_item_key_to_cpu(path->nodes[0], &found_key,
 					      path->slots[0]);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `fs/btrfs/tree-log.c`**
- The function `replay_dir_deletes` was modified to handle errors returned by the `btrfs_next_leaf()` function.
- A new condition was added to check if `ret` is less than 0, which indicates an error. If this condition is met, the function will now jump to the `out` label to handle the error appropriately.
- The existing condition that checks if `ret` equals 1 was retained, which breaks the loop if there are no more leaves to process.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The modifications ensure that the function `replay_dir_deletes` correctly identifies and responds to errors during the directory delete replay process. By adding the error handling for negative return values from `btrfs_next_leaf()`, the patch prevents the function from incorrectly setting the return value (`@ret`) to 0 when an error occurs, thus allowing the caller to be aware of the error condition. This change enhances the robustness of the error handling in the Btrfs filesystem's directory deletion replay logic.
